text: Preface A dictionary of place-names depends heavily on the myriad works devoted to the subject which have been published over many decades and acknowledgement is therefore due to their authors and researchers.
text_raw:
Preface 
A dictionary of place-names depends heavily on the myriad works devoted to the subject which 
have been published over many decades and acknowledgement is therefore due to their authors 
and researchers.

text: Introduction Over 8,000 names from around the world appear in the following pages.
text_raw:
Introduction 
Over 8,000 names from around the world appear in the following pages.

text: They cover continents, geographical regions (such as the Maghreb and South-East Asia), countries, administrative units (cantons, counties, departments, districts, divisions, governorates, prefectures, provinces, regions, republics, states and territories), bays, capes, cities, towns, deserts, islands, lakes, mountains, rivers, ruins, oceans, and seas.
text_raw:
They cover continents, 
geographical regions (such as the Maghreb and South-East Asia), countries, administrative units 
(cantons, counties, departments, districts, divisions, governorates, prefectures, provinces, 
regions, republics, states and territories), bays, capes, cities, towns, deserts, islands, lakes, 
mountains, rivers, ruins, oceans, and seas.

text: The focus has been on the more important of these, although a few lesser known names have been included.
text_raw:
The focus has been on the more important of these, 
although a few lesser known names have been included.

text: Regrettably there is no space for such place-names as Compton Pauncefoot, Middle Wallop, Rolling Fork and Scratch Ankle.
text_raw:
Regrettably there is no space for such 
place-names as Compton Pauncefoot, Middle Wallop, Rolling Fork and Scratch Ankle.

text: Names whose meaning is self-explanatory have been omitted unless there has been a good reason to include them (see Newcastle).
text_raw:
Names 
whose meaning is self-explanatory have been omitted unless there has been a good reason to 
include them (see Newcastle).

text: In looking through this dictionary it is readily apparent that many places share the same name, although the spelling may not be identical: there are at least 31 places or features called Victoria in nineteen different countries.
text_raw:
In looking through this dictionary it is readily apparent that many 
places share the same name, although the spelling may not be identical: there are at least 31 
places or features called Victoria in nineteen different countries.

text: In the USA, for example, one can find twelve cities called Athens, nine Berlin, four London, four Madrid, eight Paris, and five called Rome.
text_raw:
In the USA, for example, one 
can find twelve cities called Athens, nine Berlin, four London, four Madrid, eight Paris, and five 
called Rome.

text: Many other European names recur in North and South America, often after the birthplace of the founder.
text_raw:
Many other European names recur in North and South America, often after the 
birthplace of the founder.

text: This dictionary does not claim to be definitive or comprehensive, aims that are impossible to achieve.
text_raw:
This dictionary does not claim to be definitive or comprehensive, aims that are impossible to 
achieve.

text: Quite often there is no satisfactory etymology for a place-name and therefore no precise meaning can be established, at least at the moment; or its origins are clouded in the mists of time.
text_raw:
Quite often there is no satisfactory etymology for a place-name and therefore no precise 
meaning can be established, at least at the moment; or its origins are clouded in the mists of 
time.

text: It is almost impossible to provide a definitive derivation for some Native American and African names.
text_raw:
It is almost impossible to provide a definitive derivation for some Native American and 
African names.

text: Despite considerable research the meaning of London, for example, is not known.
text_raw:
Despite considerable research the meaning of London, for example, is not 
known.

text: Nevertheless, this does not mean that various theories cannot be put forward; some of these depend on intriguing, and sometimes entertaining, legend.
text_raw:
Nevertheless, this does not mean that various theories cannot be put forward; some of 
these depend on intriguing, and sometimes entertaining, legend.

text: This, however, is usually a poor basis for discovering the truth, Rome being a classic example.
text_raw:
This, however, is usually a poor 
basis for discovering the truth, Rome being a classic example.

text: The danger is that, popularly, the name is derived from the legend or a person, often mythical, associated with it and it is this ‘folk etymology’ that is remembered.
text_raw:
The danger is that, popularly, the 
name is derived from the legend or a person, often mythical, associated with it and it is this ‘folk 
etymology’ that is remembered.

text: Despite this, legends are included here where appropriate.
text_raw: Despite this, legends are included here where appropriate.

text: To add to the confusion, toponymists differ in their interpretations of the known facts while sometimes those facts conflict.
text_raw:
To 
add to the confusion, toponymists differ in their interpretations of the known facts while 
sometimes those facts conflict.

text: One can only offer the most plausible explanation based on the information available and if even this is unwise more than one explanation is presented.
text_raw:
One can only offer the most plausible explanation based on the 
information available and if even this is unwise more than one explanation is presented.

text: The study of place-names, toponymy, involves language (of which there are thought to be about 6 800 spoken today), history, and therefore personalities and peoples, geography and topography, religion and cultural tradition, politics, and even local industry; superstition, too, can play a role (see Cairo).
text_raw:
The study of place-names, toponymy, involves language (of which there are thought to be 
about 6 800 spoken today), history, and therefore personalities and peoples, geography and 
topography, religion and cultural tradition, politics, and even local industry; superstition, too, 
can play a role (see Cairo).

text: There is no populated place, however obscure, without a name.
text_raw: There is no populated place, however obscure, without a name.

text: It will have been chosen, presumably, for a particular reason, although now this may not be known.
text_raw:
It will 
have been chosen, presumably, for a particular reason, although now this may not be known.

text: The approximate date of founding, or naming in the case of a natural feature, the language, religion, and social and political attitudes of the namer, if known, may offer clues.
text_raw:
The approximate date of founding, or naming in the case of a natural feature, the language, 
religion, and social and political attitudes of the namer, if known, may offer clues.

text: However, the older the name, the more difficult it will be to discover these facts.
text_raw:
However, the 
older the name, the more difficult it will be to discover these facts.

text: A place-name is a window that can shed light on the past—from the language can be deduced who the inhabitants were at that time, where they went and who they communicated with.
text_raw:
A place-name is a window that 
can shed light on the past—from the language can be deduced who the inhabitants were at that 
time, where they went and who they communicated with.

text: Scandinavian place-names in England indicate where the Norwegian and Danish population was concentrated.
text_raw:
Scandinavian place-names in England 
indicate where the Norwegian and Danish population was concentrated.

text: Birkby, from Bretarby ‘Village of the Britons’, shows that this was a village inhabited by Britons rather than Anglo- Saxons.
text_raw:
Birkby, from Bretarby 
‘Village of the Britons’, shows that this was a village inhabited by Britons rather than Anglo- 
Saxons.

text: The migration of peoples has had a profound influence on the naming of places and features.
text_raw:
The migration of peoples has had a profound influence on the naming of places and 
features.

text: When East Prussia was overrun by Soviet forces in 1945 and the German population expelled, the northern half, annexed by the Soviet Union, was renamed Kaliningrad and its German names changed to Russian ones.
text_raw:
When East Prussia was overrun by Soviet forces in 1945 and the German population 
expelled, the northern half, annexed by the Soviet Union, was renamed Kaliningrad and its 
German names changed to Russian ones.

text: River names, usually adopted by immigrants and left unchanged, can indicate the presence of ancient peoples: the Esera in Spain, the Isar in Germany, the Isére in France, and the Jizera in the Czech Republic advertise the existence of pre- Celtic tribes along these rivers.
text_raw:
River names, usually adopted by immigrants and left 
unchanged, can indicate the presence of ancient peoples: the Esera in Spain, the Isar in 
Germany, the Isére in France, and the Jizera in the Czech Republic advertise the existence of pre- 
Celtic tribes along these rivers.

text: Simple translation is often the key to the meaning of a name; for example, Novgorod means ‘New Town’ in Russian, Los Angeles ‘The Angels’ in Spanish, and Shanghai ‘ By the Sea’ in Chinese.
text_raw:
Simple translation is often the key to the meaning of a name; for example, Novgorod means 
‘New Town’ in Russian, Los Angeles ‘The Angels’ in Spanish, and Shanghai ‘ By the Sea’ in Chinese.

text: It is not always as easy as this.
text_raw: It is not always as easy as this.

text: Some places have names whose meaning is not readily apparent from their current form, having evolved over time.
text_raw:
Some places have names whose meaning is not readily apparent 
from their current form, having evolved over time.

text: To try to ascertain the present meaning it may then be necessary to go back to the original name if that is possible; this may be in a different language or use obscure or unknown words.
text_raw:
To try to ascertain the present meaning it 
may then be necessary to go back to the original name if that is possible; this may be in a 
different language or use obscure or unknown words.

text: Modification of the name may make the search more difficult.
text_raw:
Modification of the name may make the 
search more difficult.

text: There are names whose literal translation appears to be irrelevant to their situation or even have no real meaning.
text_raw:
There are names whose literal translation appears to be irrelevant to their 
situation or even have no real meaning.

text_raw:

English (Anglo-Saxon) and Old Scandinavian (Old Norse and Old Danish) origin, and from the

text: vii Introduction Celtic group of languages (Brithonic, Irish and Scottish Gaelic etc.) employed earlier (and often Latinized in written sources, but not actually changed, with the arrival of the Romans).
text_raw:
vii Introduction 
Celtic group of languages (Brithonic, Irish and Scottish Gaelic etc.) employed earlier (and often 
Latinized in written sources, but not actually changed, with the arrival of the Romans).

text: The most common Latin loan-word, castra ‘fortified place’, evolved into the Old English ceaster (Roman) camp’, ‘station’, or ‘walled town’ from which the present -chester and -caster are derived: thus, Chester, Winchester, Doncaster, and many others which indicate a former Roman protected establishment.
text_raw:
The most 
common Latin loan-word, castra ‘fortified place’, evolved into the Old English ceaster (Roman) 
camp’, ‘station’, or ‘walled town’ from which the present -chester and -caster are derived: thus, 
Chester, Winchester, Doncaster, and many others which indicate a former Roman protected 
establishment.

text: Western Europe abounds with Greek and Roman names which have been modified, perhaps because newcomers could not pronounce them correctly.
text_raw:
Western Europe abounds with Greek and Roman names which have been 
modified, perhaps because newcomers could not pronounce them correctly.

text: Mérida in Spain, for example, was developed as a retirement settlement for Roman veterans (emereti).
text_raw:
Mérida in Spain, for

text_raw:
Dedicated to 
the Emperor Augustus, it was at first called Augusta Emerita, which in due course became Mérida.

text: Some modern names have resulted from misunderstandings between explorers and indigenous peoples.
text_raw:
Some modern names have resulted from misunderstandings between explorers and indigenous 
peoples.

text: Without a knowledge of the local language it was inevitable that a word or words uttered by local people were misheard or misinterpreted.
text_raw:
Without a knowledge of the local language it was inevitable that a word or words 
uttered by local people were misheard or misinterpreted.

text_raw:
European explorers in Africa would 
sometimes ask the name of a place only to be told what it was that the locals were doing (see

A state can have more than one official language, a fact which may be reflected in its place-

text_raw:
Switzerland, for example, has three, French, German, and Italian together with the

text: To its inhabitants it is known variously as La Suisse, Die Schweiz, and La Svizzera.

To its inhabitants it is known variously as La Suisse, Die Schweiz, and 
La Svizzera.

text: The small island state of Singapore has four:
text_raw: The small island state of Singapore has four:

text_raw: Chinese, English, Malay, and Tamil.

text: For Muslims the concept of nation is less important than that of religion which they see as being divided into nations.
